items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Giardino in their response to the interviewer's question 'Who's that? Giardino.' The interviewee proceeds to talk about family members and playing music at home, showing no personal connection or interaction with Giardino.

ctx.x: No, she's about the only one that played the flute. Then she's also got a son. He's taking after the footstep of his grandfather. Excuse me. He's taking after the footstep of his grandfather. He's taking a clarinet. That's Rose's children. That's Rose's children. Did you ever play in any bands, Mr. Teal? Did you ever play in any bands? Oh, I couldn't go for that. I couldn't teach a body dancing and I couldn't dance. Ever had me. Ever had me sitting down there going for somebody else to have fun. I used to like…
I think he's dead now, I'm not sure. Who's that? Giardino. What's the name? Giardino. Yeah.

We had a lot of times, you know, at home. Like sometime my brother would get in there and my sister and the one that's living now in Oral Street, she and my sister here were two young people. All of them had already died out. My sister did it also. She'd do a piano she learned, piano she learned with Camille Nickerson. And my sister that's living on Oral Street. We often times used to get out of home and I'd get out. My sister'd come home. My brother would get his car in there. She'd get on the piano. I'd get a…
